ESB.tagline: The beating heart of modern Turkey
ESB.intro: Ankara is a sophisticated capital city that perfectly blends ancient history with a vibrant, student-friendly energy. It offers a unique window into Turkish identity, away from the tourist crowds of the coast.
ESB.didYouKnow: Ankara is famous for its unique cat breed, the Ankara Cat, which is known for its silky white fur and heterochromatic eyes.

highlights.note: The monumental mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.

highlights.title: Ankara Castle
highlights.note: Historic citadel offering panoramic city views.

highlights.title: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations
highlights.note: World-class collection of prehistoric artifacts.

highlights.title: Kızılay Square

history.overview: Ankara has been a vital crossroads for civilizations including the Hittites, Romans, and Seljuks. Its historical significance surged in 1923 when it was declared the capital of the newly founded Republic of Turkey. Today, it stands as a testament to the nation's journey from an empire to a modern secular state.

periods.description: Settled by the Hittites and later transformed into a prosperous trading hub under the Romans. The ruins of the Temple of Augustus still stand as proof of this era.
The city became an important strategic outpost for Byzantine and Seljuk rulers. Its castle walls were repeatedly reinforced to withstand frequent regional invasions.
Following WWI, Atatürk established Ankara as the capital to symbolize a clean break from the Ottoman past. It was rapidly transformed from a small town into a sprawling metropolis.

figures.role: Founder and first president of modern Turkey

tips.title: Nightlife

AYT.tagline: Where ancient history meets Mediterranean sunshine
AYT.intro: Antalya is the ultimate student escape, blending crystal-clear turquoise waters with a labyrinthine Old Town. It serves as the perfect base to explore majestic Roman ruins and vibrant nightlife without breaking the bank.
AYT.didYouKnow: The city is home to the world's best-preserved Roman theater, Aspendos, which still hosts live opera performances today.

highlights.note: Historic Old Town with Ottoman-era houses and boutique cafes.

highlights.title: Hadrian's Gate
highlights.note: An ornate Roman triumphal arch marking the city entrance.

highlights.title: Düden Waterfalls
highlights.note: Dramatic waterfalls cascading directly into the Mediterranean Sea.

highlights.title: Konyaaltı Beach
highlights.note: A massive pebble beach perfect for swimming and sunbathing.

food.intro: Antalya offers a delicious mix of fresh Mediterranean produce and traditional Turkish flavors. Street food here is affordable, filling, and perfect for students on the move.

history.overview: Founded in the 2nd century BC by the King of Pergamon, Attalus II, the city has long been a vital Mediterranean port. Throughout the centuries, it transitioned through Roman, Byzantine, and Seljuk rule, leaving behind a rich archaeological footprint. Today, it stands as a major hub where modern tourism preserves the echoes of ancient civilizations.

periods.description: Founded as Attaleia, it served as a key naval base for the kingdom of Pergamon. It later flourished under Roman rule, becoming a primary gateway to the East.
The city was conquered by the Seljuk Turks in the early 13th century. This era introduced iconic Islamic architecture that defines the city's skyline today.
Following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Antalya transformed into Turkey’s tourism capital. Massive urban development has since turned the city into a global Mediterranean hub.

figures.name: Attalus II
figures.role: King of Pergamon and founder of Antalya

figures.name: Hadrian

HER.tagline: Where ancient myths meet vibrant city life
HER.intro: Heraklion is the pulsating heart of Crete, offering an unparalleled mix of Bronze Age history and modern Mediterranean energy. It is the perfect base for students looking to balance legendary archaeological exploration with a legendary nightlife scene.
HER.didYouKnow: The Palace of Knossos was once considered a mythical labyrinth, but was proven to be the center of the advanced Minoan civilization.

highlights.note: The massive, colorful seat of Minoan power.

highlights.title: Heraklion Archaeological Museum

history.overview: Heraklion has been a vital Mediterranean crossroads for millennia, serving as a maritime hub for various empires. From its origins as the port of Knossos to its intense Venetian and Ottoman periods, the city is a layered testament to conquest and cultural exchange.

periods.description: This era defined the island as the home of Europe's oldest advanced civilization. The massive palace complex at Knossos dominated the surrounding landscape during this time.
The Venetians turned Heraklion into a formidable fortress known as 'Candia.' They constructed the massive city walls that still define the historic old town today.
Following unification with Greece in the early 20th century, Heraklion grew into a vibrant capital. It remains the educational and economic powerhouse of the island.

tips.title: Hydration
tips.note: Carry a refillable water bottle, as the public fountains throughout the city provide high-quality drinking water.

BOJ.tagline: Where the Black Sea meets urban energy.
BOJ.intro: Burgas is a vibrant coastal hub that perfectly balances industrial history with a laid-back, sun-drenched student vibe. It serves as the gateway to the southern Black Sea coast, offering sprawling sea parks, sandy beaches, and a thriving nightlife scene.
BOJ.didYouKnow: The iconic Sea Garden of Burgas features a famous 'Bridge' that stretches 300 meters into the Black Sea, serving as the city’s favorite meeting spot.

history.overview: Burgas evolved from a small fishing village into a major maritime and industrial center. Its strategic location on the coast has made it a historical crossroads for various civilizations throughout the centuries. Today, it stands as a modern cultural heart of the Bulgarian seaside.

periods.description: The region was populated by Thracian tribes and later established as a trading post by ancient Greeks. It served as a vital maritime hub connecting inland settlements to the sea.
Known as Pyrgos, it functioned as a small but significant port for trade during the Ottoman rule. It slowly grew in importance due to its sheltered bay and shipping capabilities.
The city flourished in the late 19th century following the liberation of Bulgaria. It transformed into an essential industrial port and a center for oil refining and transportation.

PDV.tagline: Europe's oldest living city awaits you
PDV.intro: Plovdiv is a vibrant student-friendly hub where ancient Roman ruins blend seamlessly with a bohemian artistic atmosphere. Its colorful Revival-era architecture and bustling cafe culture make it the perfect destination for history buffs and backpackers alike.
PDV.didYouKnow: Plovdiv is officially the oldest continuously inhabited city in Europe, with roots dating back over 8,000 years.

history.overview: Plovdiv's history spans millennia, serving as a pivotal crossroads for Thracian, Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman civilizations. This layering of cultures has left behind an unparalleled architectural legacy. Today, it stands as a testament to European persistence and cultural evolution.

periods.description: The city began as a fortified settlement known as Eumolpias. Thracian tribes built the first structures on the city's seven iconic hills.
Under Roman rule, the city became a major cultural center called Trimontium. They constructed grand stadiums, theaters, and aqueducts that still stand today.
During the 19th century, the city saw an economic boom and architectural revolution. Wealthy merchants built the ornate, colorful mansions found in the Old Town.

tips.title: Respect the hills
tips.note: Plovdiv is built on seven hills, so expect plenty of uphill walking.

AMS.tagline: Canals, culture, and endless student energy.
AMS.intro: Amsterdam is a vibrant maze of historic canals and world-class museums that pulses with youthful energy. It perfectly blends a rich artistic legacy with a forward-thinking, laid-back modern lifestyle.
AMS.didYouKnow: Amsterdam is built on millions of wooden poles driven into the soft marshy ground to support its buildings.

history.overview: Amsterdam began as a humble 13th-century fishing village on the Amstel River. It blossomed into a global trading powerhouse during the Golden Age and remains a beacon of tolerance. Today, it stands as a major European hub for education, art, and international commerce.

periods.description: Founded as a small dam on the Amstel in the 1200s. It quickly grew into a bustling port for regional trade.
During the 17th century, Amsterdam became the world's richest trade center. Massive wealth funded the iconic canal rings we see today.
The city transformed into a global center for arts and tourism. It remains an open, liberal society known for innovation.

BTS.tagline: The charming capital with a pulse
BTS.intro: Bratislava is a vibrant, compact city where medieval history meets quirky modern aesthetics along the Danube. It is the perfect budget-friendly playground for students looking for nightlife, culture, and stunning views.
BTS.didYouKnow: Bratislava is the only national capital in the world that borders two other independent countries: Austria and Hungary.

history.overview: Bratislava served as the coronation site for Hungarian kings and queens for centuries, reflecting its strategic importance. After surviving the turbulence of the 20th century, it emerged as the proud capital of an independent Slovakia in 1993. The city now seamlessly blends its imperial legacy with its contemporary identity as a modern European hub.

periods.description: Between 1536 and 1783, the city was the official capital of the Kingdom of Hungary. Elaborate royal coronations transformed the city into a lavish center of European power.
Under communist rule, the city underwent rapid industrialization and mass housing projects. This era left behind iconic, if controversial, structures like the Most SNP bridge.
Since 1993, the city has blossomed into a bustling, democratic capital. It has rapidly modernized while carefully restoring its historic old-world charm.

KSC.tagline: Slovakia's vibrant eastern gem of culture
KSC.intro: Košice is an energetic student hub where medieval architecture meets a thriving modern cafe culture. It is the perfect affordable base for travelers looking to explore the hidden charm of Eastern Europe.
KSC.didYouKnow: Košice has the oldest marathon in Europe, and the second oldest in the world, held annually since 1924.

history.overview: Košice has served as a pivotal trading crossroads for centuries, shifting between Hungarian and Czechoslovak influence. It holds the distinction of being the first city in Europe to be granted its own coat of arms. Today, it stands as a resilient intellectual center, having been named a European Capital of Culture in 2013.

periods.description: Košice became a wealthy trading town due to its strategic position on the merchant routes. The construction of the massive St. Elisabeth Cathedral began during this golden age.
As part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the city flourished as a cultural and industrial focal point. It was a major railway hub that connected the empire’s disparate regions.
Following WWII, the city expanded rapidly with new residential districts and industry. Since independence, it has rebranded as a center for tech and student-driven innovation.

EDO.intro: Edremit is a hidden gem where ancient mythology meets the pristine nature of the Kaz Mountains. It offers budget-friendly students the perfect blend of hiking adventures, therapeutic thermal springs, and serene Mediterranean beaches.
EDO.didYouKnow: The Kaz Mountains, located near Edremit, are mentioned in Homer's Iliad as the place where Zeus watched the Trojan War.

history.overview: Edremit has been a crossroads of civilization since antiquity, serving as a vital port and agricultural hub. periods.description: Known as Adramytteion, it was a significant city in the Mysia region. It flourished as a center for trade under various Greek states.
The city became an important center for olive oil production during the Ottoman expansion. Its architecture reflects the traditional wooden Turkish house style.
Following the Turkish War of Independence, Edremit transformed into a modern hub for tourism and agriculture. It is now a gateway to the Kaz Mountains.

DSM.didYouKnow: The iconic gold leaf on the Iowa State Capitol dome is actually 23-karat gold, reapplied periodically by hand.

Today, it stands as a progressive capital that respects its agricultural roots while fostering a modern, innovative culture.

periods.description: Established to protect the regional territory during westward expansion. It served as a vital garrison for soldiers and traders.
The city became a coal mining and printing powerhouse by the 1900s. Infrastructure development linked the capital to national trade networks.
Recent years have seen a downtown revitalization focused on arts and technology. It is now recognized as a leading hub for finance and insurance.

VLC.didYouKnow: Valencia is the official birthplace of paella, the world-famous saffron-infused rice dish.

history.overview: Valencia was founded by the Romans and evolved into a major trade hub under Moorish influence before joining the Crown of Aragon. periods.description: Founded in 138 BC as a colony for Roman soldiers. It quickly became an important agricultural center for the empire.
Islamic rule brought advanced irrigation systems and vibrant architecture. This period deeply shaped the city's unique agricultural landscape.
Following the diversion of the Turia river, the city transformed into a green oasis. It is now a global hub for science and technology.

AXA.tagline: The vibrant heart of Caribbean tranquility
AXA.intro: The Valley is the colorful, unassuming capital of Anguilla, serving as the cultural soul of the island. It offers students a unique blend of quiet colonial heritage and authentic local island life away from the high-end resorts.
AXA.didYouKnow: The Valley was named for its location in a central depression that runs across the island, serving as the main hub for the local population.

highlights.title: Wallblake House
highlights.note: A historic 1787 plantation house reflecting island heritage.

highlights.title: Crocus Bay
highlights.note: A scenic, tranquil beach perfect for snorkeling and swimming.

highlights.title: The Old Court House
highlights.note: An iconic structure representing the island's legislative history.

highlights.title: Anguilla National Trust
highlights.note: A great hub for learning about island conservation efforts.

food.intro: Anguillan cuisine is defined by fresh Atlantic seafood and bold Caribbean spices. It’s a delicious, high-quality culinary experience that captures the essence of the ocean.

dishes.name: Johnny Cakes
dishes.note: Classic fried flour dough, a staple side for every meal.

dishes.name: Grilled Crayfish
dishes.note: Local rock lobster served fresh with garlic butter.

dishes.name: Conch Stew
dishes.note: Slow-cooked savory shellfish served in a spiced broth.

dishes.name: Peas and Rice
dishes.note: A flavorful blend of pigeon peas and seasoned rice.

history.overview: The Valley has served as the administrative center since the British colonial period began in the 17th century. Its history is shaped by early plantation economies and the 1967 Anguillian Revolution, which defined the modern national identity. Today, it remains the seat of governance and a living museum of island resilience.

periods.description: Settled by British colonists in 1650, the area functioned mainly through plantation agriculture. African enslaved laborers built the foundation of the local economy during this era.
The 1960s brought major political unrest as Anguilla sought independence from St. Kitts. The island successfully pursued its path to becoming a British Overseas Territory.
The Valley has evolved into a quiet capital that prioritizes heritage tourism and local community pride. It balances modernization with the preservation of colonial-era architecture.

figures.name: Ronald Webster
figures.role: Leader of the 1967 Anguillian Revolution

figures.name: John Coke
figures.role: Early settler and plantation owner

tips.title: Transport
tips.note: Rent a small car or moped to navigate the island's interior effectively.

tips.title: Budgeting
tips.note: Visit local roadside stalls for affordable and authentic Caribbean snacks.

tips.title: Respect
tips.note: Always ask permission before taking photos of locals or private residences.

tips.title: Sun Safety
tips.note: The Caribbean sun is intense, so keep hydrated and wear high-SPF sunscreen.

phrases.meaning: Hanging out or relaxing with friends
What is going on or how are you?

LIS.tagline: Sun-drenched hills and ancient tiled streets
LIS.intro: Lisbon is a vibrant student-friendly hub where historic charm meets a buzzing nightlife scene. Its colorful neighborhoods and steep cobblestone alleys offer an endless playground for budget-conscious explorers.
LIS.didYouKnow: Lisbon is one of the oldest cities in the world, predating Rome by several centuries.

highlights.title: Belém Tower
highlights.note: Iconic fortress guarding the harbor entrance.

highlights.title: Tram 28
highlights.note: Classic yellow tram winding through historic districts.

highlights.title: Alfama District
highlights.note: Oldest neighborhood featuring narrow, maze-like streets.

highlights.title: Bairro Alto
highlights.note: The city’s epicenter for nightlife and bars.

food.intro: Lisbon's culinary scene is a dream for students, blending affordable fresh seafood with legendary sweet treats.

dishes.name: Pastel de Nata
dishes.note: Creamy, cinnamon-dusted Portuguese egg tart.

dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás
dishes.note: Shredded salted cod with onions, eggs, and potatoes.

dishes.name: Sardinhas Assadas
dishes.note: Traditional charcoal-grilled sardines, best enjoyed in summer.

dishes.name: Bifana
dishes.note: A simple, savory pork sandwich on crusty bread.

history.overview: Lisbon has evolved from an ancient Phoenician outpost into a global maritime powerhouse during the Age of Discovery. The city survived a catastrophic 1755 earthquake that completely reshaped its urban landscape into the neoclassical grid seen today. It remains a resilient capital that honors its seafaring roots while embracing contemporary European culture.

periods.description: Lisbon was under Islamic rule for centuries, shaping its architecture and street layouts. You can still see remnants of this influence in the Alfama district.
The city became the heart of global trade, funding voyages that connected Europe to the Americas and Asia. This era brought immense wealth and grandeur to the Portuguese capital.
Following the 1755 earthquake, the city was rebuilt with revolutionary seismic-resistant architecture. This period defined the symmetrical aesthetic of the Baixa district.

figures.name: Vasco da Gama
figures.role: Famed explorer who discovered the sea route to India.

figures.name: Fernando Pessoa
figures.role: Iconic modernist poet and literary legend.

tips.title: Walk everywhere
tips.note: Wear comfortable sneakers as the city is incredibly hilly and cobbled.

tips.title: Use public transport
tips.note: Buy a Viva Viagem card to save significantly on metro and tram fares.

tips.title: Late dinner culture
tips.note: Expect restaurants to be lively well past nine in the evening.

tips.title: Free views
tips.note: Seek out the 'miradouros' (viewpoints) for the best sunset spots without paying a cent.

LAQ.tagline: The green mountainside oasis of Libya
LAQ.intro: Al Bayda, known as Al Albraq, sits elegantly in the lush Jebel Akhdar highlands. It is a refreshing escape from desert heat, offering a unique blend of mountainous landscapes and ancient heritage.
LAQ.didYouKnow: Al Bayda translates to 'The White' and is named after a white-washed mosque that once served as a landmark for travelers.

highlights.title: Cyrene Ruins
highlights.note: Ancient Greek archaeological site nearby.

highlights.title: Jebel Akhdar
highlights.note: Stunning green mountain ranges for hiking.

highlights.title: Appolonia
highlights.note: Historic coastal ruins of the Cyrenaican port.

highlights.title: Local Souq
highlights.note: Traditional market filled with regional crafts.

food.intro: Libyan cuisine in the highlands features hearty, traditional Berber-influenced dishes. Expect bold spices, fresh olive oil, and communal dining experiences.

dishes.name: Bazeen
dishes.note: Barley dough served with a rich, spicy tomato stew.

dishes.name: Usban
dishes.note: Traditional stuffed sausage filled with herbs and meat.

dishes.name: Sharba Arabiya
dishes.note: A thick, comforting Libyan soup with lamb and mint.

dishes.name: Asida
dishes.note: Soft wheat flour dough served with honey and oil.

history.overview: The region surrounding Al Bayda has been a crossroads of civilizations for millennia, from Greeks to Romans and Arabs. Its strategic location in the Green Mountains made it a crucial site for trade, religion, and regional resistance throughout history. Today, it stands as a significant educational and cultural center in eastern Libya.

periods.description: Founded as part of the Cyrenaican kingdom, the area thrived under Greek influence. It became an essential intellectual hub near the famous city of Cyrene.
Following the arrival of Arab tribes, the region adopted Islamic traditions and architecture. This era solidified its status as a center for Sufi learning.
The city gained prominence during the 20th century as a key administrative hub. It played a significant role in Libya's post-independence development.

figures.name: Omar Mukhtar
figures.role: Iconic Libyan resistance leader against Italian colonialism.

figures.name: Battus I
figures.role: Founder of the ancient Greek colony of Cyrene.

tips.title: Dress Respectfully
tips.note: Wear modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees.

tips.title: Stay Hydrated
tips.note: Always carry bottled water, especially when hiking the mountains.

tips.title: Local Connectivity
tips.note: Purchase a local SIM card for better navigation access.

tips.title: Respect Photography
tips.note: Always ask permission before taking photos of local people.

BGF.tagline: The vibrant pulse of Central Africa
BGF.intro: Bangui is a city of remarkable resilience situated on the banks of the winding Oubangui River. It offers intrepid travelers a raw, authentic look at African culture, characterized by lush landscapes and spirited local markets.
BGF.didYouKnow: Bangui is known as the 'Bangui la Coquette' due to its scenic riverfront location and abundant flowering trees.

highlights.title: Oubangui River
highlights.note: Crucial waterway offering scenic boat trips at sunset.

highlights.title: Boganda Museum
highlights.note: Exhibits on regional ethnography and indigenous traditions.

highlights.title: Notre-Dame de Bangui
highlights.note: An iconic cathedral showcasing unique colonial architecture.

highlights.title: PK5 Market
highlights.note: A bustling hub for authentic crafts and textiles.

food.intro: The local culinary scene revolves around fresh river fish and hearty staples like cassava and peanut-based sauces.

dishes.name: Kanda
dishes.note: Fried balls made from pumpkin seeds and fish.

dishes.name: Foutou
dishes.note: Pounded yam or plantain served with savory soup.

dishes.name: Maboké
dishes.note: Fish slow-cooked in banana leaves with spices.

dishes.name: Chikwangue
dishes.note: Fermented cassava dough wrapped in leaves.

history.overview: Bangui was established as a French military outpost in 1889, growing into the capital of a nation deeply influenced by its colonial past. Throughout the 20th century, the city transitioned from a colonial administrative center to the heart of the newly independent Central African Republic. Today, it remains a focal point for the country's ongoing political and cultural evolution.

periods.description: Founded by French explorers as a fort on the river. It quickly became an important strategic hub for river trade.
Gained sovereignty in 1960 under the leadership of Barthélémy Boganda. This period marked the emergence of a distinct national identity.
The city has navigated significant political volatility and unrest. It continues to strive toward stabilization and urban development.

figures.name: Barthélémy Boganda
figures.role: First Prime Minister and father of independence

figures.name: Jean-Bédel Bokassa
figures.role: Controversial leader who proclaimed himself Emperor

tips.title: Local Transport
tips.note: Always agree on taxi fares before starting your journey.

tips.title: Photography
tips.note: Do not take photos of government buildings or military personnel.

tips.title: Hydration
tips.note: Stick exclusively to bottled or treated water throughout your stay.

tips.title: Dress Code
tips.note: Dress modestly to show respect for local customs and traditions.

BLJ.tagline: The gateway to Algeria's ancient past
BLJ.intro: Batna is a vibrant city nestled in the Aurès Mountains, serving as the cultural heart of the Berber people. It is the perfect base for students looking to explore world-class Roman ruins and breathtaking mountainous landscapes.
BLJ.didYouKnow: Batna is located near the ancient Roman city of Timgad, which is famously known as the 'Pompeii of Africa' due to its exceptionally preserved grid layout.

highlights.title: Timgad
highlights.note: UNESCO-listed Roman city featuring remarkably preserved ruins.

highlights.title: Lambaesis
highlights.note: Ancient military outpost once home to the Third Augustan Legion.

highlights.title: Ghoufi Canyons
highlights.note: Stunning cliffside dwellings offering spectacular hiking and photography.

highlights.title: Belezma National Park
highlights.note: A protected mountain forest perfect for trekking and nature.

food.intro: The local cuisine in Batna is hearty and soulful, heavily influenced by traditional Berber cooking methods and local mountain ingredients.

dishes.name: Chakhchoukha
dishes.note: Flatbread torn into pieces with spicy red meat stew.

dishes.name: Kesra
dishes.note: Traditional crispy, round semolina flatbread served with olive oil.

dishes.name: Bourak
dishes.note: Crispy fried pastry rolls stuffed with meat or cheese.

dishes.name: Berkoukes
dishes.note: Hand-rolled semolina pasta served in a rich tomato broth.

history.overview: Batna evolved from a French military outpost founded in 1844 into a bustling modern city. Its deeper historical significance lies in its role as a strategic center for both the Roman Empire and the subsequent Berber kingdoms. Today, it stands as a symbolic hub for the Algerian War of Independence.

periods.description: The region was a critical agricultural and military hub for the Roman Empire. Iconic cities like Timgad and Lambaesis were established to secure the frontier.
The Aurès mountains served as a stronghold for Berber resistance against various invaders. This era solidified the unique cultural identity of the region.
Founded by the French as a garrison town, Batna later became the starting point for the 1954 Algerian War of Independence.

figures.name: Mustapha Ben Boulaid
figures.role: Leader of the Algerian revolution

figures.name: Kahena
figures.role: Warrior queen who resisted Arab conquests

tips.title: Dress modestly
tips.note: Respect local customs by dressing conservatively, especially when visiting rural areas.

tips.title: Hire a guide
tips.note: Getting a local guide for Timgad will greatly enrich your historical understanding.

tips.title: Pack for weather
tips.note: Mountain temperatures drop significantly at night, so bring layers even in spring.

tips.title: Carry cash
tips.note: Always keep small denominations of local currency for markets and cafes.

ASM.tagline: Africa's secret jewel of modernist architecture
ASM.intro: Asmara is a breathtaking high-altitude city known for its impeccably preserved 1930s Italian modernist architecture. It offers students a unique blend of African hospitality and European-influenced urban design.
ASM.didYouKnow: Asmara is nicknamed 'Piccola Roma' (Little Rome) and is a UNESCO World Heritage site for its extensive collection of futurist and art deco buildings.

highlights.title: Fiat Tagliero Building
highlights.note: A stunning 1938 futuristic gas station shaped like an airplane.

highlights.title: Enda Mariam Cathedral
highlights.note: An iconic landmark blending Romanesque and local Eritrean styles.

highlights.title: Medebar Market
highlights.note: A vibrant industrial market where recycled scraps are transformed.

highlights.title: Cinema Impero
highlights.note: One of the world's finest examples of Art Deco cinema design.

food.intro: Eritrean cuisine is a communal experience centered around sourdough flatbread and spicy, aromatic stews.

dishes.name: Injera
dishes.note: Sourdough flatbread served as the base for all meals.

dishes.name: Zigni
dishes.note: Spicy, savory beef or lamb stew cooked with berbere.

dishes.name: Tsebhi Derho
dishes.note: Traditional spicy chicken stew served with hard-boiled eggs.

dishes.name: Buna
dishes.note: Ceremonial coffee experience served with popcorn and incense.

history.overview: Asmara evolved from a collection of villages into a significant colonial hub during the Italian occupation. Following decades of conflict, it became the capital of an independent Eritrea in 1993. Today, it stands as a preserved time capsule of 20th-century urban planning.

periods.description: The city was established as a strategic Italian colonial center in the late 19th century. Italian architects subsequently designed the city with distinct modernist features.
The city witnessed intense periods of turmoil during the long war for independence. It eventually emerged as the heart of the newly formed Eritrean state.
Asmara is now celebrated for its well-preserved historical urban landscape. It serves as a living museum of colonial history and architectural innovation.

figures.name: Isaias Afwerki
figures.role: First president of independent Eritrea

figures.name: Hamid Idris Awate
figures.role: Leader of the Eritrean liberation movement

tips.title: Photography
tips.note: Always ask permission before taking photos of government buildings or people.

tips.title: Dress Code
tips.note: Dress modestly to respect local customs and traditional values.

tips.title: Connectivity
tips.note: Internet access can be limited, so download offline maps before arriving.

tips.title: Currency
tips.note: Carry physical cash as credit cards are rarely accepted.

GRZ.tagline: The charming gateway to Styrian life
GRZ.intro: Feldkirchen bei Graz perfectly blends peaceful village vibes with convenient access to the bustling cultural hub of Graz. It serves as an ideal base for students looking to experience authentic Austrian hospitality away from the city crowds.
GRZ.didYouKnow: The municipality is home to the Schwarzlsee, a massive recreational lake created from a former gravel pit that now hosts major international music festivals.

highlights.title: Schwarzlsee Recreation Center
highlights.note: Huge lake with swimming, wakeboarding, and summer festivals.

highlights.title: Austrian Sculpture Park
highlights.note: Expansive outdoor garden filled with modern art installations.

highlights.title: Graz Airport Spotting
highlights.note: Watch planes take off from the unique terrace.

highlights.title: St. Marein Church
highlights.note: Historic local church showcasing traditional regional architecture.

food.intro: The dining scene focuses on hearty, farm-to-table Styrian classics served in cozy, traditional family-run inns.

dishes.name: Steirisches Backhendl
dishes.note: Traditional breaded and fried crispy chicken.

dishes.name: Kürbiskernöl Salat
dishes.note: Fresh greens drizzled with nutty pumpkin seed oil.

dishes.name: Brettljause
dishes.note: Rustic wooden platter of local cold cuts and cheeses.

dishes.name: Apfelstrudel
dishes.note: Classic pastry filled with sweetened spiced apples.

history.overview: Feldkirchen evolved from a small agricultural settlement into a vital logistics and transport hub for the Graz region. Its historical identity is rooted in the fertile lands of the Mur river valley, maintaining its heritage while adapting to modern infrastructure needs. It remains a bridge between historical rural traditions and contemporary urban development.

periods.description: For centuries, the area relied on farming and grain production due to the fertile Mur river soil. It existed as a quiet satellite to the growing influence of nearby Graz.
The construction of the airport and infrastructure projects transformed the landscape in the 20th century. This era moved the village toward a more modern, service-oriented economy.
Today it serves as a dynamic residential community with a strong focus on recreation and regional tourism. It balances its historical village charm with the needs of a mobile population.

figures.name: Franz Schwarzl
figures.role: Entrepreneur who developed the iconic recreation lake.

figures.name: Archduke Johann
figures.role: Patron of Styrian culture and local regional development.

tips.title: Rent a Bike
tips.note: Cycling is the most efficient way to travel between the village and Graz city center.

tips.title: Check the Calendar
tips.note: Look up festival dates at Schwarzlsee to avoid crowds or book early for events.

tips.title: Use Local Buses
tips.note: Public transit links to Graz are frequent and affordable for students with valid IDs.

tips.title: Sunday Closures
tips.note: Remember that most grocery stores in town close on Sundays, so plan your shopping ahead.

OSS.tagline: The ancient crossroads of the Silk Road
OSS.intro: Osh is a vibrant, multi-ethnic gateway where ancient history meets the rugged beauty of the Pamir Mountains. It offers student travelers an authentic, budget-friendly glimpse into Central Asian culture, bustling bazaars, and legendary hospitality.
OSS.didYouKnow: Osh is one of the oldest cities in Central Asia, with historical roots tracing back over 3,000 years to the bronze age.

highlights.title: Sulaiman-Too Mountain
highlights.note: A sacred UNESCO World Heritage site overlooking the city.

highlights.title: Osh Bazaar
highlights.note: A massive, chaotic, and sensory-rich traditional market.

highlights.title: The Silk Way Museum
highlights.note: Located inside a cave within the sacred mountain.

highlights.title: Lenin Statue
highlights.note: One of the few remaining massive Soviet-era monuments.

food.intro: The food scene in Osh is dominated by hearty nomadic traditions and rich, spice-laden Central Asian influences.

dishes.name: Osh Plov
dishes.note: Signature rice dish with carrots, meat, and garlic.

dishes.name: Samsa
dishes.note: Flaky pastries filled with spiced meat or pumpkin.

dishes.name: Laghman
dishes.note: Hand-pulled noodles served in a savory vegetable broth.

dishes.name: Kurut
dishes.note: Small, salty, dried yogurt balls, perfect for trekking.

history.overview: Osh has served as a pivotal hub on the Silk Road for millennia, facilitating trade between East and West. It has shifted through the hands of various empires, from nomadic khanates to the Soviet Union. Today, it stands as a cultural capital, reflecting the complex historical tapestry of Southern Kyrgyzstan.

periods.description: The city emerged as a major center for caravan trade in the Fergana Valley. It was historically regarded as a holy place by travelers seeking blessings before mountain crossings.
Osh flourished as a significant Islamic intellectual and commercial node during the Middle Ages. It became a renowned destination for pilgrims visiting the sacred Sulaiman-Too.

The city became part of the Soviet Union in the 20th century, undergoing massive urbanization and industrialization. Following independence in 1991, it reasserted itself as a center for Kyrgyz culture.

figures.name: Babur
figures.role: Founder of the Mughal Empire and poet.

figures.name: Sulaiman
figures.role: Biblical prophet honored at the sacred mountain.

tips.title: Dress modestly
tips.note: Keep shoulders and knees covered, especially when visiting local mosques.

tips.title: Carry cash
tips.note: Most bazaars and transport options operate strictly with local som.

tips.title: Negotiate prices
tips.note: Bargaining is expected and welcomed when shopping at the bazaar.

tips.title: Download maps
tips.note: Offline maps are essential for navigating the maze-like city streets.

WSI.tagline: Sun-soaked harbors and vibrant urban energy
WSI.intro: Sydney is a breathtaking blend of iconic architecture and pristine golden beaches, offering a laid-back lifestyle for students. It balances high-energy city life with a world-class outdoor culture that is perfect for exploration.
WSI.didYouKnow: The Sydney Opera House roof tiles are not white; they are actually a subtle combination of glossy white and matte cream.

highlights.title: Sydney Opera House
highlights.note: An architectural masterpiece on the harbor front.

highlights.title: Bondi Beach
highlights.note: Australia's most famous stretch of golden sand.

highlights.title: Sydney Harbour Bridge
highlights.note: Climb the steel arch for panoramic city views.

highlights.title: The Rocks
highlights.note: Historic cobbled lanes with markets and pubs.

food.intro: Sydney’s culinary scene is a diverse melting pot influenced by fresh local seafood and strong Asian and Mediterranean roots.

dishes.name: Meat Pie
dishes.note: A classic Aussie handheld pastry filled with gravy.

dishes.name: Avocado Toast
dishes.note: The quintessential Australian cafe breakfast staple.

dishes.name: Lamington
dishes.note: Sponge cake dipped in chocolate and coconut flakes.

dishes.name: Barramundi
dishes.note: A popular, buttery white fish native to Australia.

history.overview: Sydney began as the ancestral land of the Gadigal people before becoming the site of the first British penal colony in 1788. Over two centuries, it transformed from a harsh convict outpost into a thriving multicultural metropolis. Today, it stands as a global hub of innovation and cultural heritage.

periods.description: The Gadigal people inhabited the Sydney basin for at least 30,000 years. They lived in harmony with the harbor and surrounding bushland.
In 1788, the First Fleet arrived, establishing the colony as a place of exile for British convicts. Life was brutal as settlers struggled to adapt to the harsh terrain.
Post-WWII migration transformed the city into a multicultural society. Today, it is recognized globally for its iconic landmarks and booming economy.

figures.name: Arthur Phillip
figures.role: First Governor of New South Wales

figures.name: Jørn Utzon
figures.role: Architect of the Sydney Opera House

tips.title: Public Transport
tips.note: Get an Opal card or use contactless payment for easy access to trains, buses, and ferries.

tips.title: Sun Safety
tips.note: The sun is incredibly strong, so always wear sunscreen and a hat.

tips.title: Walking Tours
tips.note: Join free walking tours to discover hidden alleyways and local history.

tips.title: Water Access
tips.note: Carry a reusable bottle as Sydney has excellent free water refill stations everywhere.

phrases.meaning: You're welcome or it is fine
